title: The Courier Is Here, but There’s No Kitchen Ticket. What Now?
summary: A courier is waiting and the kitchen has no ticket. Check the order status, avoid duplicate prep, and know when to escalate.
body_markdown:
A courier at the counter is a reason to check an order, not a reason to start cooking.


Find the exact order for your location in the merchant tool your team uses. If it’s active, check whether the kitchen already started it before using your approved fallback. If you can’t verify that it’s active and still awaiting pickup, hold the handoff and escalate.


## Start with the order ID and store


Ask for the marketplace and order ID. In the merchant order view, select the right location and match the ID and current status. For DoorDash, also check the assigned Dasher when the merchant view shows one. Don’t rely on a first name or the courier’s screen alone. Give the courier an honest update: “I’m checking the order with the kitchen. I’ll let you know when I have an update.”


[DoorDash’s Business Manager guide](https://merchants.doordash.com/en-us/learning-center/live-order-management) shows where to check active orders, their status and the assigned Dasher. On another marketplace, use the live merchant order view available for your store.


## If the order is active, find out where it stopped


Check the POS, kitchen display or printer, then ask the line and check the pickup shelf. A missing printout does not mean the kitchen never received the order. If it’s already in prep or staged, don’t enter a replacement. Verify the label against the order and follow the normal pickup process.


If the order is active, still awaiting pickup, unstarted and absent from the kitchen, have the shift lead use the store’s approved backup process once. Assign one person to own it. If there’s no approved backup or the order can’t be fulfilled as placed, use the marketplace’s support workflow. Don’t mark an order ready just to move the queue.


For some integrations, a tablet can display the order without being a supported way to accept it.[DoorDash’s Open API guidance](https://developer.doordash.com/en-US/docs/marketplace/faq/order/) describes the tablet as a backup for viewing and says tablet fallback for failed POS routing must be specially configured.


## If you can’t confirm an active order, don’t remake it


If the ID doesn’t match, the order is canceled, or your team can’t find it in the approved view, don’t hand over a similar-looking bag or start a second order. Have the shift lead escalate through the platform’s merchant support with the location, order ID, timestamp and observed status. Keep the courier updated without promising a remake or assigning blame.


Example (illustrative):


A courier asks for order 581 at the downtown store. The merchant view shows it’s active, but the printer is empty. A line cook finds it on the kitchen screen. Leave the existing ticket in place and finish that order.


After service, use[Voosh’s restaurant opening checklist](https://www.voosh.ai/blogs/restaurant-opening-checklist-delivery-apps) to rehearse your approved backup path. For a separate issue, seeing whether a storefront is online or offline, explore[Voosh Marketplace Store Uptime](https://www.voosh.ai/marketplace-store-uptime) . Store status doesn’t verify individual orders or kitchen tickets.
